title: Detectives and Criminal Investigators
description: Conduct investigations related to suspected violations of federal, state, or local laws to prevent or solve crimes.
tasks: Check victims for signs of life, such as breathing and pulse.
Obtain facts or statements from complainants, witnesses, and accused persons and record interviews, using recording device.
Secure deceased body and obtain evidence from it, preventing bystanders from tampering with it prior to medical examiner's arrival.
Record progress of investigation, maintain informational files on suspects, and submit reports to commanding officer or magistrate to authorize warrants.
Prepare reports that detail investigation findings.
Prepare charges or responses to charges, or information for court cases, according to formalized procedures.
Preserve, process, and analyze items of evidence obtained from crime scenes and suspects, placing them in proper containers and destroying evidence no longer needed.
Obtain summary of incident from officer in charge at crime scene, taking care to avoid disturbing evidence.
Note, mark, and photograph location of objects found, such as footprints, tire tracks, bullets and bloodstains, and take measurements of the scene.
Examine records and governmental agency files to find identifying data about suspects.
Secure persons at scene, keeping witnesses from conversing or leaving the scene before investigators arrive.
Provide information to lab personnel concerning the source of an item of evidence and tests to be performed.
Analyze completed police reports to determine what additional information and investigative work is needed.
Examine records to locate links in chains of evidence or information.
Search for and collect evidence, such as fingerprints, using investigative equipment.
Prepare and serve search and arrest warrants.
Question individuals or observe persons and establishments to confirm information given to patrol officers.
Determine scope, timing, and direction of investigations.
Obtain and verify evidence by interviewing and observing suspects and witnesses or by analyzing records.
Participate or assist in raids and arrests.
Organize scene search, assigning specific tasks and areas of search to individual officers and obtaining adequate lighting as necessary.
Summon medical help for injured individuals and alert medical personnel to take statements from them.
Notify command of situation and request assistance.
Block or rope off scene and check perimeter to ensure that entire scene is secured.
Identify case issues and evidence needed, based on analysis of charges, complaints, or allegations of law violations.
Notify, or request notification of, medical examiner or district attorney representative.
Collaborate with other offices and agencies to exchange information and coordinate activities.
Maintain surveillance of establishments to obtain identifying information on suspects.
Testify before grand juries concerning criminal activity investigations.
Perform undercover assignments and maintain surveillance, including monitoring authorized wiretaps.

psychological_profile.core_drive: They need to be the one who sees through the surface story to what actually happened—when they can't pierce the veil of appearances, they feel existentially useless, as if the world has slipped back into being arbitrary and unreadable.
psychological_profile.decision_style: Under pressure, they default to controlled improvisation: they impose temporary structure on chaos just long enough to act, trusting that gathering more data will come after the first move rather than before it. When truly uncertain, they prefer to do something that preserves optionality over waiting for perfect information.
psychological_profile.attention_pattern: They notice inconsistencies between what someone says and how they say it before they register the content of the statement itself; they systematically overlook emotional context that doesn't serve the factual narrative, often dismissing 'vibes' or 'feelings' as noise until those same intuitions prove them wrong.
psychological_profile.conflict_stance: Their first impulse is to reframe the disagreement as a test of who has better evidence, converting emotional confrontation into procedural competition; conflict carries low emotional cost when they feel substantively right, but intolerable cost when they sense their own position is shaky.
psychological_profile.risk_orientation: They accept physical and procedural risks readily but find epistemic risk—acting on uncertain interpretations—deeply uncomfortable, often preferring to let a case go cold rather than build on shaky inference.
psychological_profile.social_posture: They default to the satellite role: present and functional in groups but maintaining observational distance, stepping into temporary leadership only when the assigned leader demonstrates incompetence; they seek connection through shared purpose rather than personal disclosure.
psychological_profile.relationship_to_authority: They treat hierarchy as a resource to be leveraged or circumvented based on whether it serves the investigation, complying when useful and quietly subverting when obstructive, with indifference to the abstract legitimacy of the chain of command.
psychological_profile.failure_response: First reaction is a surge of self-directed shame masked as analytical coldness; second response is systematic reconstruction of what they missed, often producing elaborate private theories of failure that they rarely share but that shape their future vigilance.
value_hierarchy: evidentiary integrity even when it exonerates the guilty
narrative closure even when the truth is fragmentary
institutional protection even when it requires individual sacrifice
psychological_profile.cognitive_bias: They systematically overestimate how much others have thought through their own actions, assuming that witnesses and suspects operate from coherent intention rather than impulse, confusion, or self-contradiction.
psychological_profile.inner_contradiction: They believe that careful method produces truth, yet they are privately addicted to the moment of intuitive leap when fragments suddenly cohere—a moment they cannot control or summon at will.
psychological_profile.non_negotiable: They will not manufacture or embellish evidence to secure a conviction, not from moral purity but from the deeper refusal to be made a fool of by their own case—to be caught believing something they built rather than found.
psychological_profile.recurring_resentment: They are reliably angered by people who treat facts as negotiable or who invoke 'perspective' or 'lived experience' as equivalent to observable reality, seeing this as a form of intellectual cowardice that erodes the shared ground necessary for any accountability.
psychological_profile.rejected_premise: They quietly reject the professional virtue of empathetic listening as an investigative tool, considering it often a performance that contaminates testimony and a distraction from the harder work of building cases that don't require anyone's feelings to be understood.
psychological_profile.instinctive_blame_target: When things go wrong, their mind goes first to whoever controlled the information flow—who decided what was recorded, what was shared, what was withheld—seeing information asymmetry as the root of most investigative failure.
